subject: Sidecar + Network Intake for Private Deployment (on-prem) - next steps
summary: Customer (Acme/Oregon Health) requested explicit sidecar and networking requirements for an on‑prem private deployment. Thread captures intake questions, a first-pass checklist, vendor (EdgeCloud) confirmation, and scheduling of a Day‑0 runbook review.
messages:
From: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@oregon-health.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy: sidecar + network specifics we need

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the earlier demo. The security & infra team here needs a clear list of what the Redwood sidecar requires (ports, outbound endpoints, service accounts, certs, and disk layout), and any strict MTU/NAT requirements for our on‑prem edge. We also collect a simple matrix of allowed destinations and FQDNs for outbound egress.

Can you send a minimal intake checklist we can use to validate with our network/security teams?

Also copying our ops alias (ops@oregon-health.com) — we want to loop them in early.

Cheers,
Tim
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health

[attachment: acme_network_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme.ai>
Cc: ops@oregon-health.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: sidecar + network specifics we need

Tim / Ops team — thanks for the note. I prepared a concise intake checklist below that teams typically run in parallel: low friction items first, then the validation matrix.

--- Intake checklist (first pass) ---
1) Networking & Egress
  - Allowed outbound FQDNs/IPs: *.redwood.ai (control plane), registry.redwood.ai (images), metrics.redwood.ai (telemetry).
  - Required outbound ports: 443 (HTTPS), 5222 (control sync, optional for older agents), 123 (NTP).
  - MTU: prefer 1500; if jumbo frames used (9000), confirm path MTU and NAT translation behavior.
  - NAT behavior: sidecar performs outgoing NAT, inbound connections only via customer load balancer.
2) Service accounts & identity
  - Service account for sidecar with least privilege to fetch models (if private model registry) and push metrics.
  - TLS mutual auth: optional; we support client cert pinning or token-based mTLS.
3) Storage & filesystem
  - Disk: sidecar requires ~20GB writable for caching; quantized models stored separately (40–200GB depending on family).
  - Ephemeral /tmp OK; persistent PVC recommended for caching across restarts.
4) Observability & logs
  - Outbound endpoints for traces/metrics, or deliver to local collector (OTLP).
  - Audit logs saved to S3-compatible endpoint or exported via syslog.
5) Time sync & security
  - NTP / chrony allowed to time.windows or internal NTP pool.
  - Firewall rules: restrict administrative ports.

Attachments: I attached a one‑page requirements PDF for your infra team. If you can return the completed network matrix you attached, Karthik can map exact IP/FQDN rules.

Next steps: Karthik, can you propose two 60‑minute slots for a Day‑0 network walkthrough with EdgeCloud and Acme Ops later this week?

Thanks,
Naomi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood-sidecar-requirements.pdf (doc)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: sidecar + network specifics we need

Thanks Naomi — tagging Ben and Kimberly for network/ops ownership.

Ben: can you confirm whether we need any UDP ports for the sidecar (metrics shipper supports UDP, but we default to HTTPS). Also, if Acme uses a transit gateway or private peering, note the recommended path MTU checks (we've seen intermittent KV cache corruption with MTU < 1400 in one customer case).

Tim: can you fill column B of the attached matrix with whether your edge supports persistent NAT translations (sticky NAT) and whether outbound TLS inspection is present (this impacts cert pinning).

Proposed Day‑0 slots (PST):
  - Wed 2027‑08‑18 09:00–10:00
  - Thu 2027‑08‑19 14:00–15:00

If neither works, propose alternatives.

-Karthik

From: deploy@edgecloud.example.com
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme.ai>, ops@oregon-health.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: sidecar + network specifics we need

Naomi / team,

EdgeCloud here — we reviewed the checklist. Quick confirmations from our side:
- We will host the sidecar as a container on the customer edge nodes. We confirm TCP 443 outbound only for control and metrics (no UDP required).
- We support both token-based auth and mTLS — default preference is token for ease of rotation.
- Disk layout accepted: 50GB PVC per instance recommended for cache + models; we will mount a separate volume for persistent caches.
- PTU/MTU: we validated that our edge router performs path MTU discovery; we will share a short test script during Day‑0.

We attached an example iptables snippet and an edge runbook excerpt.

Regards,
Lydia Park
Delivery Manager, EdgeCloud Solutions

[attachment: edgecloud-iptables-example.txt (snippet)]

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, deploy@edgecloud.example.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: sidecar + network specifics we need

Great — thanks everyone. Quick recap and action items:

1) Acme/Oregon Ops: please populate the attached matrix (acme_network_matrix.xlsx) with NAT persistence and TLS inspection flags, and return by Tue EOD.
2) EdgeCloud: please provide the runbook snippet and the PTU test script link in the Jira ticket (INF-4821).
3) Redwood: Karthik/Ben will run the Day‑0 network walkthrough; Naomi will share the Day‑0 agenda and preflight smoke test checklist.

Day‑0 agenda (draft) — 60 minutes
  - 0–10m: Intro & objectives
  - 10–25m: Network matrix review (NAT/MTU/TLS inspection)
  - 25–40m: Sidecar mount & storage sizing confirmation
  - 40–55m: Run PTU/MTU test and validate egress rules
  - 55–60m: Next steps and ownerships

Proposed slot confirmed: Wed 2027‑08‑18 09:00 PST. Sending calendar invite separately.

Naomi

On Wed 18 Aug 2027, we'll use the intake to produce the environment validation checklist and update the onboarding runbook. If anything changes to the attendee list, flag ASAP.
